clue.text: Cuts the chat about…

definitions.note: a verb: to chop with a small axe

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trims away idle conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THE CHAT. 'Cuts' is the verb sense: to chop with a hand axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small axe, and in verb use it means to chop or hack.

clue.text: The ram's turned into a rodent

indicators.note: turned into means transformed, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale transformation of a male sheep into a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small burrowing rodent kept as a pet.

clue.text: Inter a king, foully murdered, in the ground…

indicators.note: a violently mangled body suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Bury a monarch who was killed treacherously.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land or ground considered for its physical features.

clue.text: … thought to be responsible for such pains?

definitions.text: … thought to be responsible for such pains?

parts.words: … thought to be responsible for such pains?
parts.note: aches in the head, where thought happens

explanation.surface: Asking what is blamed for these aches.
explanation.walkthrough: The pains come from the place where thinking takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Pains felt in the head, the seat of thought.

clue.text: Amherst folks doctor this bottle of drink

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: People in Amherst, Massachusetts, spike a drinks bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum-insulated bottle that keeps drinks hot or cold.

clue.text: … those who draw and shoot farmers

definitions.meaning: people who pull back a bowstring and loose arrows
the family of a long-running BBC radio soap set on a farm

explanation.surface: Marksmen with bows open fire on rural folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera about a farming family in the fictional village of Ambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen draw and shoot; the soap's title family are farmers.

clue.text: The German takes it to British army, all up and dressed…

indicators.note: in a down entry, every piece written upwards reads backwards

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A German man joins the British reserves, fully kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all up' turns DERITTA as a whole, upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired means clothed or dressed in particular garments.

clue.text: …with half of Manchu navy providing their morning milk?

indicators.note: only the last three of the six letters of the word are kept

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A Chinese sailor supplying breakfast milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A churn is the large can in which milk is delivered from the dairy.

clue.text: He likes to eat mince pie with foreign cleric

indicators.note: mincing chops something up, so the letters are chopped into a new order

parts.note: curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A foodie enjoys mince pie with a priest from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person who delights in fine food.

clue.text: It's Fay's turn to be content

indicators.note: a turn changes the order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fay is satisfied when her go comes round.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to content or please them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Rear sheep by entrance to resort

indicators.note: to rear is to rise up backwards, so the word for the sheep is turned around

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Raising livestock beside a field entrance near a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a farming verb but turns RAM backwards. Margate is a seaside resort town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a traditional English seaside holiday town.

clue.text: Sometimes his views on holidays are outlandish

definitions.text: Sometimes his views on holidays are outlandish

parts.words: Sometimes his views on holidays are outlandish
parts.note: a holidaymaker abroad looks at foreign, literally outlandish, sights

explanation.surface: A man's opinions about vacations can be bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlandish' reads as 'eccentric' but literally means 'of foreign lands', the sights a holidaymaker sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer on holiday views scenery in other countries.

clue.text: Jeweller's circle headed by aristocratic woman

definitions.text: Jeweller's circle headed by aristocratic woman

parts.words: Jeweller's circle headed by aristocratic woman
parts.note: a jewelled ring worn on the head of a noble lady

explanation.surface: A group of jewellers led by a noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circle' suggests a social group, and 'headed' its leader; in fact it is a ring of jewels on a lady's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headdress worn by duchesses and princesses.

clue.text: See rum&gin mixed with sugar &egg-whites

indicators.note: the letters are stirred together like a cocktail into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: combine spirits with sugar and egg whites.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringues are confections of whisked egg white baked with sugar.

clue.text: The American spreads beef on them

definitions.text: The American spreads beef on them

parts.words: The American spreads beef on them
parts.note: large US cattle farms, 'spreads', carry beef cattle

explanation.surface: A US diner smears beef on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like a verb but is a noun: in America a big farm is a spread, and beef cattle graze it.
explanation.definitionFit: American cattle farms are called spreads and raise beef herds.

clue.text: Yearned to rebuild church house

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the same bricks together in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone longed to reconstruct a building belonging to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A deanery is the official residence of a cathedral dean.

clue.text: Old imperial possessions whose founders started from London docks!

definitions.text: Old imperial possessions whose founders started from London docks!

parts.words: Old imperial possessions whose founders started from London docks!
parts.note: the colonies on the far side of the globe settled by convicts shipped from London

explanation.surface: Former colonies founded by men who set sail from London's docks.
explanation.walkthrough: Australia and New Zealand, settled partly by transported convicts who sailed from the London docks; 'docks' also hints at the convicts in the court dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Places diametrically opposite Britain on the globe, chiefly Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Advanced form of security!

parts.note: money paid in advance as a guarantee

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge kind of safety system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' suggests sophisticated, but it means paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A down payment handed over beforehand acts as a guarantee.

clue.text: Ties on the fronts of these seats

definitions.text: Ties on the fronts of these seats

parts.words: Ties on the fronts of these seats
parts.note: bow ties, false shirt-fronts and rear carriage seats all share the name

explanation.surface: Fastenings on the front of some chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: A dickey is a bow tie, a detachable shirt front, and an extra seat at the back of a carriage or old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickey covers a bow tie, a false shirt front and a folding seat.

clue.text: Rude person's dog?

parts.note: pointing at people is rude, so such a person is one who points; also a gun dog

explanation.surface: Asking what breed an impolite owner keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: It is rude to point, so a rude person might be called one who points, which is also a breed of gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a hunting dog that stands still aiming at game.

clue.text: If he gives away his land, he may be charged…

definitions.text: If he gives away his land, he may be charged…

parts.words: If he gives away his land, he may be charged…
parts.note: betraying one's country leads to a charge of treason

explanation.surface: A landowner who donates his estate may face a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives away' suggests a gift but means betrays; 'charged' suggests a fee but means accused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who betrays his country faces prosecution for treason.

clue.text: Travels free for miles or knots

definitions.meaning: to hitch is to thumb lifts from passing drivers
ties in rope, such as a clove hitch

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker travelling without paying, or a sailor's rope ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhiking gives free journeys, and a hitch is also a kind of knot.

clue.text: … and strung up in can for practising blood sports

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: hung means suspended or executed by hanging
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Something suspended in a tin for hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting is the pursuit of animals for sport, a blood sport.

clue.text: One getting free sum of money being paid by relatives

definitions.text: One getting free sum of money being paid by relatives

parts.words: One getting free sum of money being paid by relatives
parts.note: a captive released once family pay a ransom

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a free cash gift from family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting free' suggests a handout, but means being released once a ransom is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held until a ransom is paid by the family.

clue.text: Where children put their friends up when they come down to play

definitions.text: Where children put their friends up when they come down to play

parts.words: Where children put their friends up when they come down to play
parts.note: playground boards that lift one child as the other drops

explanation.surface: Hosting young friends who visit for a playdate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put their friends up' suggests giving them a bed, but it means lifting them in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesaws are pivoted planks on which children rise and fall in turn.

clue.text: I fetch in a rude potentate

indicators.note: rude in the sense of crude or rough, so the letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A rough servant brings something to a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the ruler or leader of a clan or tribe.

clue.text: See 4
Ship on a river carrying Oriental lawmen

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the Po is the major river of northern Italy
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A vessel on a river with an Eastern passenger aboard, carrying law officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is a link here; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Part of the surplus is disembowelled cat

parts.note: extra means additional, over the amount needed

indicators.note: with its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Gruesome: some of the leftovers are a gutted cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disembowelled' removes the middle of CAT, leaving CT.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage or portion taken from a larger work.

clue.text: State consumed by the First Lady of Wales?

parts.note: something consumed by another is in it
Diana, Princess of Wales, the leading royal woman of that title

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nation was swallowed by a Welsh princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana was Princess of Wales from 1981 to 1996, hence 'First Lady of Wales'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: One kicking-or kicking his heels

definitions.meaning: a footballer who shoots at goal
idling, as a worker on strike does

explanation.surface: A man who kicks, or one waiting about idly.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward kicks the ball, and a worker who downs tools sits idle.

clue.text: Sacred writings, true up to a point

definitions.meaning: the four New Testament books of the life of Christ
'gospel' means absolutely true; the clue teases it is only partly so

explanation.surface: Holy texts that are only partly accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John are holy books, and gospel truth is unquestioned fact.
